D156 language/15-concurrency.md, stdlib/06-iterators-and-generators.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md Kyokai has no language-level async/await/futures/executors; high-concurrency I/O uses explicit Poller-based libraries.
D168 language/15-concurrency.md Child-task result/error communication uses explicit channels or synchronization; panic and TPOE are not task result values.
D183 language/15-concurrency.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md, rationale/06-concurrency.md Rendezvous channels use explicit construction and synchronous handoff; bounded channels require capacity at least one.
D212/D236 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, language/15-concurrency.md, stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md Raw capability-bearing I/O is exclusive by handle; multi-task sharing uses explicit brokers or explicit synchronized wrappers, not hidden runtime mutexes.
D235 language/15-concurrency.md Thread creation failure is explicit ThreadSpawnError at spawn or covered by pre-reserved task capacity; failed spawn transfers no captures.
D262 language/13-contracts-and-runtime-failure.md, rationale/01-language-design.md, rationale/03-error-handling-and-tpoe.md Stack overflow is runtime-fatal and must be detected or guarded before safe Kyokai memory invariants can be corrupted.
Austral goals language/01-goals-and-non-goals.md, rationale/01-language-design.md, appendices/c-austral-differences.md Compatible inherited goals are carried into Kyokai directly: simplicity, correctness, security, readability, maintainability, modularity, strictness, and restraint.
Attribution policy language/00-introduction.md, language/01-goals-and-non-goals.md, rationale/00-rationale-index.md, project/04-project-licensing.md, appendices/c-austral-differences.md Wording from Fernando Borretti’s Austral specification is marked as source text from Austral; Kyokai authorship is not attributed to Borretti; source attribution is carried directly by public prose.
Rationale policy rationale/00-rationale-index.md Rationale chapters are non-normative explanation, credit Borretti’s Austral source wording when used, and defer exact behavior to normative language, toolchain, stdlib, and appendix chapters.
Austral difference index appendices/c-austral-differences.md Kyokai indexes inherited Austral files, replacement homes, and retirement status while keeping the Kyokai spec self-contained.
D25 toolchain/06-formatter.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md kyokai fmt is deterministic, idempotent, zero-config, edition-aware, parse-preserving, and does not perform semantic rewrites.
D26 toolchain/00-toolchain-overview.md, toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/03-cli.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md The single kyokai binary uses shared manifest/workspace scope, stable commands, explicit profile/target/admitted-C-toolchain selection, stable streams, and stable exit behavior.
D28 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Inline tests, doc tests, coverage, and benchmarks run through ordinary compiler semantics and explicit harness modes.
D29 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Diagnostics have stable codes, severity, spans, JSON records, suggestions, suppression policy, deterministic ordering, and command/runner failure categories.
D31 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Build profiles, target/C-toolchain configuration, output types, link mode, native dependencies, and release artifacts are explicit configuration.

D79 language/04-modules-and-visibility.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md, toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md, toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md .koi is a versioned package interface contract artifact used for dependency checking, docs, LSP, audit, reproducibility, compatibility, and concrete KBI artifact exchange.
D80 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Target triples are legal only by explicit target matrix/spec, have support tiers, and reject unsupported target/C-toolchain combinations early.

D105 toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md, toolchain/06-formatter.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Package manifests select language edition; tools parse/check/format source by edition; .koi compatibility requires exact edition match; editions are not SemVer.

D137 toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Tests, eval, generators, and playground execution receive no ambient authority; capability-using code declares its authority and receives isolated capability instances for every declared grant.
D144 toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Incremental compilation is a package/module/query optimization with exact fingerprint invalidation and no semantic effect.
D148 toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md kyokai lsp is the official language server and shares the compiler engine, diagnostics, manifest model, and semantic checks.
D149 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Cross-compilation uses manifest-centered target tables, importable target-spec TOML, admitted C-toolchain records, and reproducible target-spec inputs.
D150 toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md, rationale/05-capabilities.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md kyokai audit reports dependency, unsafe, FFI, capability, native, generation, reproducibility, and API risk facts without changing semantics.
D151/D151a toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md kyokai eval and kyokai repl use the real compiler engine; REPL sessions are persistent and obey linear cleanup on reset/quit.
D157 toolchain/00-toolchain-overview.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Toolchain releases classify compatibility impact, use a later four-week train, and keep editions separate from ordinary releases.
D200 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md Identical-code folding is profile-controlled and allowed only when observable Kyokai behavior, debug needs, exported symbols, and provenance remain valid.
D218 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md kyokai doc produces public-interface HTML/JSON, renders contracts, extracts explicit doc tests, and supplies SemVer/audit metadata.
D219 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md kyokai test --coverage reports Kyokai-source-level coverage through LCOV and HTML outputs and fails explicitly when faithful source mapping is unavailable.
D221 toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md The official package index is a read-only discovery index and does not replace pinned source revisions.
D222 toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Lints are compiler-integrated diagnostics with tiered severity and project policy; Kyokai has no separate kyokai lint command.
D223 toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Package SemVer is an advisory API/version convention checked against public interfaces and .koi metadata, while lockfiles remain revision-based.
D225 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Official CI and release artifacts include setup support, OCI images, checksums, provenance, stable diagnostics, and portable install behavior.
D226 toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Compiler Explorer and sandbox-runner behavior are official toolchain contracts; hosted playground deployment and hostname are infrastructure choices outside stable language semantics.
D243 toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md Mixed-edition workspaces are structurally legal, .koi consumption requires exact edition compatibility, and stdlib/package evolution uses SemVer where source semantics are not changing.
D244 toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md Package yanks are append-only metadata that block new selection while preserving existing lockfile meaning unless policy rejects them.
D264 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Build outputs use kyokai-out/, disposable tool state uses .kyokai-cache/, artifacts are partitioned by target/profile/package and C-toolchain identity where required, and clean/override behavior is explicit.
D265 toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md, toolchain/03-cli.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md .koi uses the canonical KBI-1 binary container with required sections, exact compatibility fields, canonical hashing, and official verify/print/diff commands.
D266 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md kyokai init and kyokai new create deterministic project templates with explicit manifests, module roots, and non-destructive behavior.
D267 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Diagnostic explanations are shipped locally through kyokai explain; kyokai fix applies only validated machine-applicable-safe suggestions by default, while less-safe classes require explicit action or remain advisory.
D268 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md kyokai --version and kyokai doctor expose Kyokai toolchain identity, host setup, target/C-toolchain support, and common setup failures without requiring a project.
D269 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Package remove/search/info/tree/why/outdated/vendor workflows are specified as read-only inspection or explicit pinned offline materialization commands.
D270 toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, rationale/08-toolchain-philosophy.md Property and fuzz testing include seed, replay, corpus, minimization, list, and failed-test rerun controls with reproducible report artifacts.
D302 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md Observability is explicit and sink/capability-shaped; standard event records, profile hooks, allocator events, and non-semantic hot/cold hints are specified.
D303 toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md Kyokai has a first-party Analysis Server with LSP as one frontend, sharing compiler facts and exposing borrow, linearity, capability, lowering, .koi, unsafe, and generated-provenance views (amended by D537/D538: derived-interface sync against .koi replaces interface/body sync).
D304 toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md Property tests, benchmarks, fixtures, fuzz targets, replay records, corpus workflow, and CI reports are first-class toolchain/test artifacts.
D305 stdlib/00-stdlib-overview.md, stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md The standard library has Core, Systems, Extended, Experimental, and Internal tiers with admission and stability rules.
D306 project/04-project-licensing.md, README/license docs The existing D263 license boundary is stated explicitly: toolchain GPL-3.0-or-later, runtime/stdlib/target helpers GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC Runtime Library Exception 3.1, no legal-advice wording.
D307 project/02-decision-traceability.md, PROJECT_STANDARDS.md, Kyokaishape.md, phase.md Public D-point workflow accepts issue/discussion/PR starts, Lead YES, reverse maturity indexing, distinct version axes, and phase/status-board tracking without making phase.md normative.
D308 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md Build identity, local cache correctness, cache-aside artifact validation, debug path policy, admitted external compiler flags, stack defaults, and incremental no-semantic-effect rules are accepted shape.
D309 stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md, stdlib/07-math-and-numerics.md, stdlib/10-crypto-policy.md RIIK requires safe native Kyokai where evidence is strong, FFI for hard external domains, small audited unsafe kernels, math/crypto oracles, and admission evidence.
D310 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md Capability attenuation derives weaker sealed capabilities through explicit APIs; manifests are audit/policy inputs; semaphores, permits, bounded slots, and rate-limit tokens are ordinary explicit linear stdlib capability or synchronization values.
D311 toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md .koi/KBI has canonical sections, provenance, target and C-toolchain compatibility identity where materialization requires it, hard error cases, and official publish-time interface diff enforcement.
D272 toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, toolchain/03-cli.md Package discovery uses Git-hosted or static signed metadata; ordinary Git source identity remains canonical and private indexes remain explicit configuration.
D273 toolchain/09-reproducibility-incremental-builds.md, toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md An immutable package cache or proxy is content-hash keyed, verifies source identity, and never replaces vendoring or lockfile-pinned Git identity.
D274 toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, stdlib/10-crypto-policy.md Advisories use typed signed records with affected ranges, fixed revisions, embargo handling, and explicit policy promotion.
D275 toolchain/03-cli.md Daily package and build mutation commands are explicit, scope-bounded, plan-reporting operations with dry-run behavior where mutation is prepared.
D276 toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md The manifest schema is TOML-based with explicit workspace inheritance, target-conditioned dependencies, additive features, and sandboxed generation declarations.
D277 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md External-tool failures become Kyokai diagnostics; debug/profile workflows are first-party lanes; eval and REPL start without root authority.
D278 language/12-implicit-completions-and-elaboration.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md The compiler-owned implicit-completion registry is closed and checked against the resolved package, typeclass, and .koi graph before inserted operations are trusted.
D279 language/07-generics-and-typeclasses.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md Typeclass coherence uses the orphan boundary, gives unsafe modules no exemption, records instances in .koi, and rejects visible conflicts before code generation.
D280 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, language/15-concurrency.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md Generic user types are task_local by default; task_transfer structural explicitly requests post-substitution stored-field classification; opaque, unsafe-backed, target-backed, and foreign-backed types need explicit unsafe transfer contracts; .koi records the resulting facts.
D281 language/15-concurrency.md Spawn failure is recoverable at the spawn site, starts no child, creates no synchronization edge, and leaves would-be captures available to the failure arm.
D283 language/15-concurrency.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md Poller readiness waiting remains distinct from channel select; registration, readiness, rearm, cancellation, and timeout behavior are explicit protocol states.
D284 language/15-concurrency.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md Every blocking or cancellable primitive publishes NoEffectOnCancel, PartialProgress, ConsumesOnCancel, or UncancellableBlocking, plus its race and ownership-commit rule.
D285 language/13-contracts-and-runtime-failure.md, language/10-statements-and-control-flow.md Panic runs eligible structured cleanup, while TPOE and runtime-fatal termination run no arbitrary user cleanup.
D286 language/08-patterns.md, language/10-statements-and-control-flow.md, language/11-linearity-borrowing-and-regions.md Refutable pattern sugar lowers to explicit case before linearity checking; every success, failure, loop, and early-exit path accounts for linear payloads.
D287 stdlib/06-iterators-and-generators.md, language/11-linearity-borrowing-and-regions.md Borrowed iterator items carry iterator-tied or named regions; for-in creates a fresh per-iteration borrow region; drain/owning iterators are exhausted, returned, or explicitly finalized.
D288 stdlib/03-allocators-and-memory-containers.md, stdlib/05-collections.md, language/11-linearity-borrowing-and-regions.md Collections containing linear elements expose hole-free safe APIs; uninitialized-slot tracking stays inside audited storage internals.
D289 language/07-generics-and-typeclasses.md, language/11-linearity-borrowing-and-regions.md, stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md Destroyable[T] names manual domain cleanup and Cleanable[T] names generic container/drain cleanup. Free values satisfy cleanup without runtime work; Linear values require named consuming implementations; neither protocol runs automatically at scope exit.
D291 language/05-declarations.md, language/06-type-system.md, language/09-expressions-and-evaluation.md Tuple types, tuple literals, tuple destructuring, and anonymous multiple returns are rejected; nominal records and nominal recovery values carry multi-field state.
D292 language/13-contracts-and-runtime-failure.md, stdlib/02-core-result-optional-display-error.md Error conversion is explicit and fatal reports use structured payload fields without turning panic, TPOE, or runtime-fatal termination into catchable exceptions.
D293 language/10-statements-and-control-flow.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md Must-use and intentional-discard diagnostics distinguish visible free-value discard from illegal linear discard.
D294 language/18-built-ins.md, stdlib/07-math-and-numerics.md Numeric operations state overflow, division, remainder, shift, NaN, infinity, signed-zero, rounding, and conversion behavior explicitly.
D295 language/05-declarations.md, language/09-expressions-and-evaluation.md, language/18-built-ins.md Compile-time evaluation is deterministic, budgeted, host-effect-free, and macro-free.
D296 language/18-built-ins.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Embedding and static assertions are explicit compile-time inputs and checks; verification helpers remain tooling views rather than alternate language semantics.
D297 toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md, stdlib/11-transitional-ffi-tracking.md Codecs, schema tools, and bindgen run through declared generation or wrapper-kit records; token macros do not enter Kyokai source semantics.
D299 language/17-memory-layout-and-backend-contract.md, toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md Platform behavior is selected-target-defined through explicit target contracts; cross-target gaps reject instead of silently changing safe semantics.
D301 language/11-linearity-borrowing-and-regions.md, language/17-memory-layout-and-backend-contract.md, stdlib/03-allocators-and-memory-containers.md Pinning, emplacement, stack storage, and large arrays preserve visible movement, layout, and initialization rules without hidden relocation assumptions.
D313 language/03-grammar.md, language/04-modules-and-visibility.md, language/05-declarations.md, toolchain/02-module-resolution-and-koi.md Grammar closure keeps the single .kyo module source (amended by D537/D538); public declarations are importable, while modules whose declarations are all private or internal publish no public API.
D315 language/00-introduction.md, rationale/01-language-design.md, README and public guide work Adoption and comparison material is public documentation work and does not replace normative chapters.
D318 language/06-type-system.md, language/07-generics-and-typeclasses.md, language/12-implicit-completions-and-elaboration.md Generic variance, nested inference, and closure storage follow closed local elaboration and ownership rules instead of open-ended inference.
D319 project/03-formalization-roadmap.md Proof tooling and formal models do not add dependent source-language semantics; proof claims use named evidence tiers.
D320 toolchain/03-cli.md, toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md, language/19-examples.md Examples, local installation, CLI extensions, and migrations use official toolchain lanes with the same compiler engine and explicit compatibility boundaries.
D323 language/03-grammar.md, language/05-declarations.md, language/16-unsafe-ffi-and-abi.md bitrecord declarations and bit access expose explicit layout, width, access, and target-contract behavior for register-oriented code.
D324 stdlib/03-allocators-and-memory-containers.md Arena APIs expose allocator ownership, region coupling, reset invalidation, bulk teardown, and failure behavior explicitly.
D326 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md, language/16-unsafe-ffi-and-abi.md Safe thread-local storage is keyed and capability-gated; ambient thread-local variables and raw TLS shortcuts stay outside safe code.
D330 language/18-built-ins.md, stdlib/02-core-result-optional-display-error.md Rich formatting is typed and protocol-driven; allocating and streaming forms retain explicit allocator and I/O failure contracts.
D331 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, toolchain/03-cli.md, language/19-examples.md Beginner scaffolds can generate visible authority plumbing but never inject hidden capabilities, allocators, cleanup, or imports.
D332 toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/03-cli.md Workspace discovery and manifest precedence are deterministic and explicit; tools do not infer package ownership from arbitrary folder layout.
D334 language/17-memory-layout-and-backend-contract.md, stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md Small unsafe or optimized kernels require a real contract, target boundary, evidence, and audit record; meme-status shortcuts create no admission path.
D335 language/18-built-ins.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md Embedded assets are explicit compile-time inputs included in build identity and grant no runtime filesystem authority.
D336 language/18-built-ins.md, stdlib/02-core-result-optional-display-error.md Built-in formatting forms lower through one canonical protocol identity rather than hidden alternative formatting semantics.
D337 language/02-lexical-syntax.md, language/03-grammar.md, language/04-modules-and-visibility.md, language/09-expressions-and-evaluation.md, language/12-implicit-completions-and-elaboration.md receiver function is the exact receiver-callable export marker; receiver-call syntax is UFCS elaboration over visible declarations, and fallback resolution does not invent hidden method lookup.
D338 language/06-type-system.md, language/07-generics-and-typeclasses.md, stdlib/03-allocators-and-memory-containers.md User-defined Auto classification examines substituted stored fields, union payloads, and captured environment fields; phantom and const arguments affect classification only through stored-component rules; recursion uses a monotone fixed point; allocator dispatch stays explicit.
D339 language/06-type-system.md, language/12-implicit-completions-and-elaboration.md, language/18-built-ins.md Never lifting is closed and local to admitted joins; it does not create general subtyping or variance.
D410 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md Atomic file updates use filesystem or narrowed directory authority; temp resources, replacement, sync policy, no-follow behavior, TOCTOU exposure, cross-filesystem rejection, advisory locks, and linear lock-guard lifetime are explicit.
D415 toolchain/07-testing-coverage-bench.md, stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md Allocation-failure testing records deterministic injection policy, affected allocator class, observed failure path, and cleanup evidence.
D416 toolchain/10-package-index-semver-releases-ci.md, stdlib/01-admission-contracts.md Behavioral compatibility checks include stdlib contracts, failure classes, ownership, capability requirements, and interface artifacts rather than names alone.
D417 stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md Process APIs separate spawn/setup failure from the linear child handle and return structured ProcessStatus values with explicit live-child cleanup policy.
D512 CODE_STANDARDS.md, PROJECT_STANDARDS.md, tracked compiler-architecture work Compiler directory separation is a review and ownership boundary; it does not claim the implementation refactor already exists.
D513 PROJECT_STANDARDS.md, docs/infrastructure/services.md, tracked website and infrastructure work Reused OSS infrastructure requires license compatibility, attribution, provenance, local-change records, and removal of foreign branding or semantics.
D521 docs/infrastructure/services.md, tracked website work Website page families are routed by role: normative spec, guides, toolchain docs, stdlib docs, package docs, examples, security, releases, community, showcase, and governance.
D523 PROJECT_STANDARDS.md, docs/contributing/spec-writing.md Public spec writing follows the maintained contract-matrix, no-maybe, traceability, review, and PR/MR workflow guide.
D341 language/10-statements-and-control-flow.md, language/18-built-ins.md Inclusive ascending range loops use endpoint-before-successor semantics so max-endpoint loops do not perform hidden overflow arithmetic.
D342 language/15-concurrency.md, stdlib/09-concurrency-primitives.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md Channel select ... pick; stays separate from Poller/readiness wait ... wake;, with shared arm tables for transfer, cancellation, deadline, and fairness diagnostics.
D343 language/13-contracts-and-runtime-failure.md, language/18-built-ins.md, toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md Runtime termination has explicit normal-exit, panic, TPOE, and runtime-fatal categories, with ExitCode, backtrace policy, stack defaults, and fatal-hook ABI rules.
D344 stdlib/04-text-bytes-paths-and-strings.md, language/16-unsafe-ffi-and-abi.md, stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md Span/SpanMut are region-bound borrowed views; dynamic library handles are linear and symbols are tied to the library borrow and ABI contract.
D345 toolchain/04-build-profiles-targets-linking.md, language/13-contracts-and-runtime-failure.md, language/16-unsafe-ffi-and-abi.md Freestanding targets define startup, memory, interrupt, allocator, fatal, linker, volatile/MMIO, and no-OS capability contracts explicitly.
D346 language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md, stdlib/08-io-files-env-process-time-random.md Capability authority is compiler-owned through sealed capability declarations and .koi facts; stdlib APIs expose concrete capability-bearing handles without owning the semantics.
D347 stdlib/02-core-result-optional-display-error.md, language/09-expressions-and-evaluation.md Result combinators preserve callable ownership, allocator behavior, must-use diagnostics, and StandardError source/diagnostic interaction explicitly.
D348 language/11-linearity-borrowing-and-regions.md, toolchain/05-diagnostics.md The checker-visible ownership states are Live, SharedBorrowed(n), MutBorrowed, PartiallyMoved(field-set), Moved, Consumed, and PendingLoopConsumption; deferred cleanup registration is separate reservation metadata.
D349 language/07-generics-and-typeclasses.md, language/09-expressions-and-evaluation.md, language/12-implicit-completions-and-elaboration.md Expected-type flow is local and fixed-order; literals, nested generic calls, Never lifting, completions, and instance selection have deterministic elaboration edges.
D350 language/16-unsafe-ffi-and-abi.md, language/15-concurrency.md, language/14-capabilities-and-authority.md Foreign callback registration is unsafe-contract-covered and states ABI, lifetime, thread affinity, reentry, capability transfer, fatal behavior, and unregister synchronization.
D351 toolchain/01-manifest-package-workspace.md, toolchain/11-build-generation-and-playground.md, toolchain/08-docs-lsp-audit.md [generate] and [audit] are declarative manifest schemas for external tools, provenance, environment policy, trust, and reproducible command inputs/outputs; no build-script DSL exists.

Formalization Roadmap

[Rikona Kurasaki / Mjoyufull] > ProofTrace: SPEC-APPENDICES-D-FORMALIZATION-ROADMAP > Covers: This chapter is registered in the public ProofTrace evidence graph; registration does not claim implementation, conformance, or theorem completion.

This project chapter records the formalization plan and current public evidence. Kyokai’s sequential ownership core has a Gate-B paper-proven theorem for the narrow lambda_K-seq boundary. Mechanization remains scheduled after self-hosting.

Trace: D143/D241, D394, D477 Covers: Kyokai requires a paper proof for the sequential core before v1.0, keeps zero-UB claims scoped to named evidence tiers, and schedules later mechanized proof work after self-hosting.

Proof Scope

The first calculus is lambda_K-seq: a small sequential core for ownership, borrowing, moves, regions, linear consumption, pattern binding, control-flow joins, checked failure, and TPOE. It deliberately excludes concurrency, FFI, backend lowering, package resolution, the full stdlib, and toolchain behavior.

Trace: D143/D241, D90, D245 Covers: The first formalization is sequential and excludes concurrency, FFI, backend, and stdlib/toolchain layers.

Required Paper Artifact

The paper proof must define abstract syntax, typing judgments, store/ownership state, borrow-region state, small-step operational semantics, checked failure/TPOE outcomes, progress, preservation, and the exact theorem statement for the safe sequential core. Any gap must be named as an assumption or excluded feature.

Trace: D73, D143/D241 Covers: The paper proof must specify syntax, typing, semantics, failure outcomes, and soundness theorem scope.

Milestones

Milestone Output Status Meaning
Scope freeze Feature list for lambda_K-seq with exclusions. The calculus knows what it is proving.
Core syntax Abstract syntax for expressions, statements, owners, borrows, regions, and failure forms. Surface syntax is not required; elaborated core is enough.
Static judgments Typing, ownership, borrowing, movement, region, and control-flow join judgments. The checker rules have a proof-facing shape.
Dynamic semantics Small-step semantics with store, ownership state, and named failure outcomes. Evaluation behavior is explicit.
Soundness theorem Progress/preservation adapted to linear ownership and TPOE. The theorem says what cannot go wrong and what may terminate.
Paper proof Human-checkable proof document. Required before v1.0.
Mechanized plan Lean 4 selection, pinned Elan toolchain, Lake build, and encoding strategy. Lean 4 is selected. Whole-core mechanization remains after self-hosting.
Early checked artifact Narrow Lean spot lemmas for the owner-slot runtime repair. Selected carrier, branch-frame, region-exit, retained-writer, and suspended-call-boundary facts are mechanically checked without claiming whole-core soundness.

Trace: D143/D241 Covers: Formalization work proceeds through explicit artifacts instead of vague proof intent.

Relation To Maintained Artifacts

kyokaicalculus/scope.md freezes the first theorem boundary, and kyokaicalculus/claim-tiers.md defines the evidence vocabulary. The statics, dynamics, lemma inventory, derivation packages, theorem assembly, elaboration map, extension map, and later-boundary files assign each rule to its proof or non-proof treatment. kyokaicalculus/paper-proof.md carries the preservation-or-defined-failure and progress-or-defined-failure overview after the earlier substitution runtime was retired for branch-sensitive owner duplication. The revised machine keeps linear values in owner slots, selects one evaluation path through continuation frames, separates static region and lease atoms from runtime identities through explicit witness I, retains elaborated call witness phi, and limits cleanup to named consuming operations. kyokaicalculus/theorem-assembly.md composes L1-L40, L38, L39, L40, Theorem P, and Theorem Q into the Gate-B paper proof. The narrow Lean artifact checks selected repair facts mechanically without claiming whole-core Lean mechanization.

Later Extensions

After the sequential proof, later formalization work can add concurrency happens-before reasoning, task transfer, channels, cancellation, unsafe/FFI contracts, backend lowering preservation, stdlib contract models, and mechanized proof. These layers must not blur the first theorem. They extend the proof boundary only after the sequential core is stable.

Trace: D90-D101, D143/D241, D228, D245 Covers: Concurrency, unsafe/FFI, backend, and stdlib proof work are later extensions.

Proof Honesty Rule

Until a theorem is discharged, spec text may say language contract, design goal, or intended invariant. It must not claim that a paper or mechanized proof exists.

Public claims record two separate axes. The D477 semantic-scope axis is SafeCore, SafeConcurrent, SafeFFIWrapped, UnsafeModule, or BackendConforming, paired with maturity state designed, specified, mechanized, tested, or conformance_checked. The D312 proof-evidence axis is intended-by-spec, implemented-and-tested, conformance-backed, paper-proven, or mechanically-proven. A D477 maturity label never implies a D312 proof-evidence label.

A claim names its semantic scope, maturity state, proof-evidence tier, artifact path, assumptions, exclusions, and owner. D479-D487, D502, and D508 also apply: modal words cannot hide implementation freedom, and proof-relevant prose must use explicit contract tables or open a new D-point when accepted shape is incomplete. When proof work changes a rule, the normative chapter and traceability appendix must be updated in the same pass.

Trace: D143/D241, D155, D312, D477, D479-D487, D502, D508 Covers: The spec must not overclaim proof status, must classify proof evidence precisely, and must keep proof-driven rule changes traceable.

ProofTrace Evidence Graph

Trace: D526 Covers: Public evidence metadata connects normative chapters, maintained code boundaries, tests, conformance work, and proof artifacts without collapsing specification, implementation, conformance, or proof state.

Kyokai maintains kyokaiproofstatus.toml as the public source registry for the ProofTrace evidence graph. kyokaiproofstatus.md is generated from that registry. It is a public status board, not a normative language chapter and not a file edited by hand.

A ProofTrace record has one stable ID and records scope, owner, specification artifacts, implementation artifacts, test artifacts, proof artifacts, exclusions, and four separate state axes:

Axis Meaning
spec_status Whether the registered scope has normative text or remains planned.
implementation_status Whether implementation is absent, planned, inherited bootstrap code, a prototype, or implemented Kyokai behavior.
conformance_status Whether public executable conformance evidence is absent, planned, or present.
proof_status One evidence tier from kyokaicalculus/claim-tiers.md.

Every record also states proof_required = true or proof_required = false. A false value requires one closed reason category: tooling-service-behavior, workflow-only, documentation-only, infrastructure-only, bootstrap-harness, or generated-artifact-plumbing. A no-proof reason does not waive ordinary correctness, test, conformance, security, or review obligations. It states only that a theorem is not the acceptance criterion for that boundary.

Every maintained normative chapter with decision traces has one chapter-level marker:

> ProofTrace: SPEC-LANGUAGE-11-LINEARITY-BORROWING-AND-REGIONS
> Covers: This chapter is registered in the public ProofTrace evidence graph; registration does not claim implementation, conformance, or theorem completion.

Every maintained spec-relevant implementation, harness, conformance, and proof boundary has a language-appropriate source comment:

(* kyokai:prooftrace id=BOOTSTRAP-LINEARITY-CHECK *)

The marker belongs at the boundary responsible for the registered contract. It is not required on every helper beneath that boundary. When a helper becomes an independently maintained semantic, toolchain, stdlib, unsafe, backend, conformance, or proof boundary, it receives its own record and marker.

ProofTrace metadata is tooling evidence only. It cannot change parsing, type checking, ownership, borrowing, capability checks, lowering, generated code, runtime behavior, package resolution, or theorem truth. An inherited compiler pass is marked inherited-bootstrap; it is not described as Kyokai implementation evidence merely because the file exists.

toolchain/prooftrace/check_prooftrace.py validates the registry schema, status vocabulary, chapter registrations, required code-boundary comments, closed no-proof reasons, artifact paths, and generated status board. make proofstatus regenerates kyokaiproofstatus.md. make check-prooftrace and CI reject stale or malformed evidence metadata.

Bidirectional Specification And Calculus Correspondence

Every calculus rule, abstraction, lemma family, executable trace, and Lean theorem identifies the normative clauses and surface, core, or IR facts it represents or excludes. Every semantic specification change receives a proof-impact record covering mappings, definitions, lemmas, model traces, Lean artifacts, compiler IR, and claim tier. A model clarification is resolved as a normative repair, an accepted model-only abstraction in deviation.md, or a pending D-point; source meaning cannot remain proof-only.

Correspondence records bind source revision, clause IDs, calculus revision, compiler IR schema, assumptions, trusted base, exclusions, reviewer, and disposition. Impact classes are NO_SEMANTIC_IMPACT, MAPPING_ONLY, MODEL_AFFECTING, PROOF_AFFECTING, and CLAIM_INVALIDATING; each class names its minimum artifacts and reviewer role. Machine registries generate forward and reverse views across clauses, calculus rules, theorems, IR schemas, traces, conformance, and ProofTrace. Human review decides the relationship.

kyokaicalculus/findings-divergence.md is the public intake ledger. A finding closes only after every selected spec, calculus, proof, compiler, test, and claim artifact is updated and a named reviewer records its disposition. Unknown correspondence blocks the affected claim, Gate-A closure, or release claim, not unrelated compiler work.

Revision-Bound Proof Review

Every paper-proven claim names an immutable review packet bound to source commit or tree digest, theorem IDs, proof revision, model and Lean revisions, and verification commands. It records the reviewer’s display name or stable public identity, authorship relationship, relevant competence, date, scope, checklist, findings, severity, author response, repair revision, unresolved assumptions, exclusions, review class, and disposition.

maintainer, AI, community, or independent without an identified reviewer is incomplete evidence. Author review, AI-assisted review, community review, and independent qualified-human review remain distinct labels. A material proof, calculus, or spec change invalidates or narrows the old packet according to its impact record and requires a new packet or explicit carry-forward. Missing review evidence downgrades the public claim; it does not refute the theorem. ProofTrace checks packet identity and coverage, not mathematical correctness.

Trace: D580-D581 Covers: Proof claims carry reviewable two-way semantic correspondence and named revision-bound review evidence.

Calculus Model Identity And Coupled Review

Every calculus family declares a stable family ID, model epoch, monotonic revision, source digest, accepted-spec cutoff, and trusted base. Rules, judgments, lemmas, theorems, traces, executable models, and proof-assistant artifacts have stable IDs and revisions. An ID is never reused for a different statement. An incompatible change to representation, judgment form, transition relation, trusted base, or theorem interpretation advances the model epoch.

A proof review packet binds the exact statement, dependency revisions, commands, results, source/spec cutoffs, and named human reviewer. Pull requests that touch this boundary declare one class: spec_only, calculus_only, coupled_semantic, or proof_review. Applicable checks cover registries, spec-calculus correspondence, executable models, Lean, ProofTrace, clause extraction, generated views, and review-packet presence.

A calculus_only change cannot alter the meaning of a source-language claim. If it does, the change becomes coupled_semantic and cites or opens a D-point. Public issue forms can record semantic/spec findings, calculus/proof defects, correspondence drift, and proposals. A complete typed finding in the PR does not need a duplicate issue.

The release knowledge manifest pins the exact calculus and proof artifacts and their claim tiers. Monthly and release specification reviews cover the formal delta since the preceding reviewed knowledge state.

Trace: D628, D630 Covers: Formal evidence has stable semantic identity and a Git review class rather than relying on filenames or branch state.

Admission And Semantic Change Control

[Rikona Kurasaki / Mjoyufull] > ProofTrace: SPEC-PROJECT-05-ADMISSION-AND-CHANGE-CONTROL > Covers: This project chapter defines how the official Kyokai project changes closed semantic registries and admits standard-library, Bridge, provider, and compiler surfaces without turning project paperwork into language semantics.

An admission record is evidence about a named implementation or integration. It is not a language construct and cannot make an otherwise illegal program legal. The language, toolchain, or standard-library chapter states the rule; the admission record identifies the implementation, supported targets, contracts, and evidence that claim to satisfy it.

Closed semantic registries include compiler-known typeclasses, implicit completions, synchronized-sharing types, SpawnShareable entries, task-transfer classifications, unsafe primitives, built-in operators, and target/provider families whose membership affects checking or artifacts. The official project changes one of these registries only through accepted shape, updated normative text, .koi and compatibility treatment where applicable, diagnostics, conformance cases, and a reviewed implementation change. An admission record cannot add a member before the normative rule does.

Every official standard-library module, Bridge, foreign wrapper, generated binding family, compiler/toolchain tuple, platform adapter, protocol provider, cryptographic provider, runtime dataset, and application integration has its own admission identity. The record contains the applicable contract fields from the owning chapters, provenance, owner, review state, supported and unsupported targets, implementation and unsafe boundaries, test evidence, compatibility class, update policy, and withdrawal procedure.

Unsafe-origin instances and secret-, capability-, unsafe-, or foreign-backed protocol implementations receive explicit audit coverage. Bridge or generated status never makes a raw ABI declaration safe. A safe-wrapper admission points to the exact unsafe contracts and wrapper APIs that establish ownership, aliasing, lifetime, thread, callback, allocator, error-snapshot, capability, cleanup, target, and provenance obligations.

An independent implementation may use different review machinery. It cannot claim conformance after adding a semantic registry member that the applicable Kyokai specification revision does not contain. It can implement an optional or target-gated provider only within the bounds written by the owning contract.

Trace: D85, D229-D232, D245, D376, D448, D460, D499, D501, D529, D569a-D569c, D576, D584, D593a Covers: Official admission proves a named implementation claim; normative chapters alone decide language and contract membership.

Reference Products And Workload Evidence

[Rikona Kurasaki / Mjoyufull] > ProofTrace: SPEC-PROJECT-06-REFERENCE-PRODUCTS-AND-WORKLOADS > Covers: This project chapter defines the official reference products and cross-phase workloads used to pressure Kyokai’s public surfaces without treating those products as language or standard-library semantics.

After the native Kyokai toolchain, the first organization-owned reference product is a maintained long-lived Poller server. It uses only public language, standard-library, package, capability, allocator, network, and Poller surfaces. It covers HTTP Core, WebSocket, configuration, structured logs, metrics, deadlines, cancellation, bounded queues, overload, and graceful shutdown. Simulation, load, soak, malformed-input, slow-client, dependency-failure, injected-OOM, restart, upgrade, and security-boundary evidence accompanies it. The product is not whole-language conformance and cannot alter semantics by precedent.

Kyokai adopts no official game engine. SDL3 is the first serious raw game and systems Bridge workload; raylib is the first small beginner game surface after its own admission. Engine integrations identify whether they use a C ABI, native plugin, generated binding, embedded host, process protocol, or a recorded combination. Their contracts publish callbacks, affinity, lifetime, reload, allocation, failure, authority, targets, assets, and packaging behavior. No engine receives hidden garbage collection, shared ownership, backend, or source semantics.

Reference games exercise 2D rendering, fixed-step simulation, frame arenas, data-oriented/ECS and slot-map pressure, input, audio, save/load, asset reload, profiling, and deterministic replay. Godot and Unity experiments remain separately identified project work until admitted through the ordinary process.

Each cross-phase workload has an owner, exact revision, dependency and target identity, authority and resource budgets, execution cadence, evidence class, known exclusions, and claim ceiling. A workload can expose a defect or motivate a D-point. It cannot decide a new rule by becoming popular or difficult to change.

Trace: D600-D601, D620, D623 Covers: Maintained workloads test the combined design throughout development while retaining a narrower evidence class than conformance.

Austral Difference Index

[Rikona Kurasaki / Mjoyufull] > ProofTrace: SPEC-APPENDICES-C-AUSTRAL-DIFFERENCES > Covers: This chapter is registered in the public ProofTrace evidence graph; registration does not claim implementation, conformance, or theorem completion.

Kyokai is a fork, not a denial. Austral remains the source of many good bones: linear types, capability direction, explicit modules, strictness, and a readable spec tradition. This appendix maps where Kyokai carries Austral ideas forward, where it changes them, and where Borretti’s Austral wording is credited as source material instead of being presented as Kyokai authorship.

Trace: D5, D86, Attribution policy Covers: Kyokai is self-contained while preserving traceable Austral lineage and attribution.

Reader Rule

If a new Kyokai chapter and an inherited Austral file overlap, read the Kyokai chapter as the current normative home. If Borretti’s Austral wording is worth using, put it in the Kyokai chapter or rationale with a source note instead of making the reader reconcile two documents.
